text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League meeting between Newcastle United and Manchester City at St James' Park!
Newcastle have had a tough time of it in the league recently, having lost six of their last nine games in the competition (W3 D1).
They've lost their last three in a row in the Premier League, a run which followed their exit from the EFL Cup in the quarter-finals as they were beaten on penalties by Chelsea.
They did win last time out, beating local rivals Sunderland 3-0 in the FA Cup.
Eddie Howe will be hoping they can emulate their 1-0 win over City in the EFL Cup earlier this season though to get them back on track.
City are aiming to try and close the gap to leaders Liverpool to just two points, with the Reds not playing until next weekend.

After a slight blip in form, the Citizens have turned things around again, and are currently on an eight-match unbeaten run in all competitions (W7 D1), winning their last four in the league before their 5-0 FA Cup win over Huddersfield Town last time out.
They have a good record against Newcastle though, winning more games (30) and scoring more goals (98) against them than any other opponent in the Premier League.
Howe makes just one change to the side that beat Sunderland in the FA Cup last weekend, and it's an enforced one.
Joelinton picked up a thigh injury in that game, so he misses out today.
He's replaced by Miley on the left of midfield.
Pep Guardiola makes six changes from their FA Cup victory over Huddersfield last time out.
Ederson is back in goal, with Walker, Ake, Rodri, Doku and Silva, who missed that game through illness also coming in.
Ortega, Gomez, Lewis, Bobb and Grealish drop to the bench, while Manuel Akanji is out with a knee injury.
There's still no Erling Haaland either due to a foot injury.
The teams are out on the pitch now, with kick-off just moments away!
Alvarez gets the game under way for City!
NO GOAL! It's a wonderful move from Newcastle in their own half before Trippier lifts it over the top to pick out Isak's run down the right.
He squares it to Longstaff on the edge of the six-yard box and he pokes it in, but before he can even begin his celebration, the offside flag goes up.
Ederson collided heavily with Walker, who was sliding in to try and block the shot, and he's still down receiving treatment on his knee.
City aren't happy as they think this could've been avoided by raising the flag earlier as Isak was clearly offside.
WHAT A CHANCE! Ederson is back on his feet to continue, but he looks incredibly shaky.
Ake knocks it back to him, and the keeper kicks it straight at Almiron, who closes him down quickly, and Guimaraes pounces on the rebound, but he can't set up Almiron for a shot.
Ederson is back on the floor and Guardiola is screaming to his bench that a change needs to be made after that earlier mistake.
The goalkeeper throws his gloves down in frustration, and his game is coming to an early end.
Ederson limps his way off the pitch with the medical team and heads straight down the tunnel.
Ortega comes on in his place.
City are pushing forward with intent here and Doku makes a driving run inside from the left, riding two challenges before eventually running into Guimaraes.
He still tries to pick out Alvarez, but Botman cuts out the loose pass.
Newcastle have won just one of their last 32 Premier League games against City (D5 L28), beating them 2-1 at St James' Park in January 2019.
Gvardiol cuts Newcastle wide open with his throughball into Foden, and he darts into the box before pulling it back towards Alvarez on the penalty spot.
Guimaraes slides in to block it, giving away a corner which comes to nothing.
CHANCE! Almiron was caught offside just moments ago, but this time, the linesman's flag doesn't go up against him as he races down the wing.
He drills his low cross into the box for Isak, but he stumbles, sending his shot wide.
OVER! City counter quickly, with Rodri playing a wonderful throughball out to Doku on the left.
He lays it off to Kovacic, who trips over the ball, and Foden can't control it behind him either.
Silva follows in, but blazes his first-time shot over the bar.
City are upping the pressure again here, and using their width to cause Newcastle some problems.
They look to Foen on the right on this occasion, but his drilled shot is blocked by Burn's outstretched leg.
The ball is gone when Guimaraes slides in on Kovacic, and he catches the Croatian with his trailing leg.
He's shown the first booking of the game.
Newcastle have everyone apart from Isak back on the edge of their own box.
Foden can't pick out a pass from the right, so looks to Rodri, but his throughball is cut out by Botman.
There's just no space for the visitors in the final third at the moment.
Gordon knocks the ball past Dias and it looks like he has the beating of him until the defender knocks him off the side of the pitch.
The throw-in is given in City's favour, and the Newcastle fans are furious with the referee's decision.
WHAT A GOAL! It's stunning from Silva! Doku plays a wonderful switch out to Walker on the right, and he clips his cross onto the edge of the six-yard box.
Schar is tight to Silva's side, but the midfielder improvises with a brilliant backheel flick which rolls past Dubravka and into the back of the net.
1-0 City!
Walker is under absolutely no pressure from the Newcastle players when it comes to him, and he plays the cross just in time to make sure Silva won't be flagged offside.
Tempers are starting to flare a little bit here, with Newcastle feeling especially hard done by because they didn't get a free-kick for the earlier foul on Gordon.
When Guimaraes is tripped and they do get a decision, the fans sarcastically cheer the referee.
GREAT SAVE! There's so much space in behind Newcastle at the moment, and Alvarez plays a great cross in from the left to pick out Silva.
He's unmarked and hits it first time on the volley, but Dubravka gets two strong hands to it.
Almiron beats City's offside trap this time and takes it to the byline before chipping it into the middle towards Isak.
He sets himself to hit the shot, but Kovacic gets back just in time to intercept it.
CHANCE! Ortega wants too long on the ball and Isak charges him down to win the ball back.
Guimaraes unselfishly tries to tee up the Swede for a shot, but Rodri slides in with a vital challenge to put it out for a corner.
GOOD SAVE! Ortega just about gets away with an under-pressure clearance, but Burns slips when he tries to bring it down, allowing Foden to break.
He bursts down the right before picking out Silva, but he's denied at the near post by Dubravka.
ISAK EQUALISES! Schar slides in with a brilliant tackle to nick it off Doku, and when it comes to Guimaraes in the middle, he instantly sweeps it forward for Isak.
He races past Walker to reach it before checking inside and curling a delightful finish past Ortega and into the back of the net.

events.action: curling a delightful finish past Ortega

text: It's superb play from Guimaraes, who has the vision to spot Isak's run through the middle and then execute it with a perfectly-weighted pass.

GORDON SCORES! Newcastle have turned this game around in a couple of minutes! Isak steps in to nick it off Rodri on the halfway line, and the Magpies don't waste any time as Burn slides it down the left for Gordon.
He checks inside before using Gvardiol as a shield to curl his shot into the same spot as Isak only moments ago.
2-1 Newcastle!
Like Guimaraes before, Burn doesn't hold up the play by trying to take too many touches - he just gets it down the wing, setting Gordon on his way.
Doku is hovering behind Schar's shoulder, and the defender stumbles over the ball, allowing the Belgian to get in behind.
He drives into the box, but Botman is there to prevent a shot at the expense of a corner.
GOOD SAVE! City are all over the place as Isak is slipped in again.
He gets in between the two centre-backs, getting a yard on Dias to poke a shot towards goal from just inside the box, but Ortega gets behind it to smother it.
Gvardiol is too casual as he waits for Dias' pass and Trippier cuts in front of him to intercept.
He volleys a great cross towards the far post, but none of his team-mates are in the box to get on the end of it.
WIDE! Trippier dinks another good ball over the top and Almiron brings it down, dragging Ortega out to the right side of the box.
He chips his shot over the goalkeeper, but it bounces wide before the flag goes up against him once more.
We're into eight added minutes at the end of the first half as Almiron pushes forward down the right again.
He's cut off by Gvardiol, but Trippier quickly wins it back and crosses to Gordon, but he can't hit the shot cleanly.
Rodri gets caught by Guimaraes, and goes down a little dramatically, knowing the Brazilian is on a yellow card.
The referee plays the advantage, and City aren't happy when the Spaniard is pulled up for a retaliation foul on Guimaraes.
Just to add insult to injury in the visitors' minds, Rodri is booked for his foul on Guimaraes, and he's arguing with the referee about the decision.
He needs to be careful.
It looks like City are going to get in behind again as Kovacic slides it forward for Doku, but Almiron slides in with a brilliant tackle to stop the attack.
The hosts try to counter, but Trippier is caught offside.
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 2-1 MANCHESTER CITY.
Newcastle come from behind to lead City 2-1 at half-time after a great first half of football.
Longstaff was denied a goal by the offside flag after just 90 seconds, but Ederson was forced off shortly after for an injury sustained trying to save it.
Silva gave City the lead in style with a wonderful backheel flick from the edge of the six-yard box in the 26 minutes.
Two goals in just over two minutes flipped things on their head though as Isak and Gordon both curled great shots into the bottom right corner to put Newcastle in front.

events.action: curled great shots into the bottom right corner

text: Howe will be particularly pleased with how his side responded to going behind, and they arguably could've had more if they'd taken their chances.
He'll want more of the same, but they need to improve on trying to beat the offside trap.
Guardiola's frustration continued to increase as the half went on, with his side looking very disjointed after conceding twice in quick succession.
He'll be after a big improvement as they try to turn this game around.
Newcastle get us back under way for the second half!
There are big shouts for handball by the City players as they think it struck Miley's arm when he blocked Doku's cross.
The Belgian was closest to it and carries on without protest, with the referee also giving a shake of his head.
It's all City in the opening minutes here, but their final ball into the box is just letting them down at the moment.
Doku tries to play a one-two with Rodri, but the return pass is played straight to Botman, who clears his lines.
GOOD SAVE! Rodri is fouled by Burn to win a free-kick through the middle, and City aren't happy when a card isn't taken out of the referee's pocket.
Alvarez takes the set-piece, curling his shot through a gap in the wall towards the near post, but Dubravka pushes it away.
City haven't scored first and trailed at half-time in the Premier League since a 3-3 draw with Newcastle in August 2022 (2-1 down at half-time).
Silva kicks Schar's legs out from under him, getting nowhere near the ball.
The referee thinks about it for a moment before giving him a yellow card.
City are staying camped deep in Newcastle's half at the moment, but they just aren't gelling in the final third.
Rodri lifts it over the top for Gvardiol, but Trippier just does enough to stop him from nodding it down to Silva.
City have reinforcements warming up as Alvarez goes over to take a corner, but he chooses to go short to Silva.
It's a wasted opportunity for the visitors as they can't pass their way into the box once again.
After soaking up another long spell of City pressure, Trippier attempts to get his side out of their compact shape.
He drives down the right, only to be shepherded out by Gvardiol.
GREAT BLOCK! City break quickly on the counter, with Alvarez threading it into Walker at the byline.
He brushes Gordon off to pull it back into the middle, and Guimaraes takes it off his toe before poking it away from Rodri, who was following in.
GOOD SAVE! This time, City do manage to open up a pocket of space in Newcastle's penalty area as Doku pokes it into Alvarez on the left of the box.
He whips a shot on goal, but Dubravka punches it away.
It's almost too intricate from City as Kovacic slides it into Foden, who in turn picks out Doku.
Instead of trying to hit a shot first time, he tries to drag it around Schar, and the ball rolls harmlessly to Dubravka.
GOOD SAVE! Newcastle use the opportunity to move it upfield in a couple of passes, and Isak is racing onto Longstaff's cross.
Ortega reads it well though, and he rushes forward to smother it, taking the chance away from the Swede.
City's second change of the game sees the goalscorer, Silva, taken off with De Bruyne on in his place.
His first involvement is going to be taking a free-kick just outside the box.
CHANCE! De Bruyne's free-kick is straight into the wall, but Dias keeps it alive for the visitors, sending it pinballing through the box.
It bounces up nicely for Alvarez, but he leans back, sending his shot sailing over the bar.
De Bruyne is already causing problems as he links up with Foden down the right before pulling it back to Alvarez in the middle.
Burn slips trying to get across to it, but ends up in the right place to block Alvarez's first-time shot.

DE BRUYNE EQUALISES! What an impact he's had since coming on, and he's scored with just his fifth touch in the game! City win a free-kick on the halfway line, and after drawing the Magpies out of their shape, Rodri slides it forward for De Bruyne.
He makes a weaving run through the rest of Newcastle's half before taking a shot from the edge of the D and drilling it low into the far bottom corner.

events.action: drilling it low into the far bottom corner

text: It's a great throughball from Rodri into De Bruyne's feet, taking Newcastle's midfield out of the game.
Ortega hasn't coped well when put under pressure from Newcastle's front line today, and he's forced into another error as he kicks it straight out of play.
Gordon takes the throw-in quickly, but Isak can't latch onto it.
De Bruyne is being given a lot of space down the right, and after more patient build-up from the visitors, he's picked out.
He drills a low cross into the six-yard box, but it's too close to Dubravka.
De Bruyne's strike was City's 100th against Newcastle in the Premier League, the first side they've netted a century against in the competition.
City's final change sees Doku taken off, with Bobb on in his place.
GOOD SAVE! Rodri runs at Schar on the edge of the box, before dropping a shoulder to wrongfoot the defender so that he can drill a shot towards the far post.
Dubravka gets down quickly, tipping it wide.
De Bruyne swings it in with the outside of his right boot, and Dubravka has to scramble to his near post.
Alvarez tries to get under it on the line, but the keeper manages to tip it over the bar just in time.
Newcastle are making their first change now, and it's Gordon that's going off for Hall.
Still, Newcastle have no answer to De Bruyne's threat down the right, and he fizzes another dangerous cross into the middle.
Bobb is running onto it at the near post, but Botman gets in front of him to stop him from getting a tap-in.
City are pushing for a late winner as the end of the game ticks closer, but Newcastle are still standing their ground well.
They're getting bodies in the box, keeping it in the wide areas for now.

BOBB SCORES! Have City won it late on? De Bruyne floats a lovely ball over the top to pick out Bobb's run off the back of Trippier, and the youngster darts in behind him, taking it off the defender's toe before rounding Dubravka, who rushes off his line, to slot it into the empty net.

events.action: slot it into the empty net

text: It's wonderful composure, and he makes it 3-2 City!
You can't argue that the game changed with De Bruyne's introduction, and after pulling his side level, he's now assisted what could be the winner with a wonderful pass.
Almiron is adamant that the ball hit a City hand in the box, but the referee is having none of it.
Newcastle can't keep it upfield for long though, and they've only got seconds left to try and get an equaliser.
FULL-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 2-3 MANCHESTER CITY.
De Bruyne comes off the bench to help City come from behind to beat Newcastle 3-2.
The Magpies had a goal disallowed for offside inside 90 seconds, which also resulted in Ederson having to go off injured as he collided with Walker trying to make the save.
City took the lead through Silva, who scored an audacious backheel flick, but two goals in just over two minutes put Newcastle in control, with Isak and Gordon both bending in lovely finishes.
The hosts looked fairly comfortable, at least until the 69th minute when De Bruyne was introduced.

The Belgian drilled in an equaliser from the edge of the box five minutes later before picking out Bobb in stoppage time, with the youngster coolly slotting into an empty net after rounding the goalkeeper.
It's a win that moves City up to second in the table, now just two points behind Liverpool.
Next up for them is Tottenham in the FA Cup in two weeks' time.
That's now four Premier League defeats in a row for Newcastle as they stay in 10th.
They travel to Fulham for their FA Cup tie next time out.
That's all for today, goodbye!
